OCR hallucinates leading digit as 7 on the 'Total Amt Rounded' line."},{"id":"F2","description":"total_amount wrong for 077.jpg: predicted 23.25; printed final 'TOTAL: 23.25' is correct per receipt — but feedback marks this incorrect, implying oracle uses 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' (pre-rounding) as the answer."},{"id":"F3","description":"total_amount empty string for 078.jpg instead of null; also wrong value chosen in intermediate iterations (100.00 from Cash Received). Final run outputs empty string, not Python None."},{"id":"F4","description":"date wrong for 034.jpg: receipt shows 09/03/2018 (DD/MM/YYYY) but prediction is 2018-08-09, i.e. month/day swapped. Agent interpreted ambiguous '09/08/2018'-like OCR as MM/DD instead of DD/MM."}],"root_causes":[{"id":"R1","description":"Candidate selection within a priority tier uses 'last candidate wins' and does not deprioritize lines containing OCR-noise markers between keyword and amount (e.g. 'Total Amt Rounded ——S«702.00'). This causes garbage-decimal numbers to beat clean earlier matches like 'Total incl. of GST 102.00'. Cross-variant voting also fails because the same noise appears in multiple OCR variants."},{"id":"R2","description":"No cross-check between candidate total and other same-value anchors on the receipt (Subtotal / Payment / Cash paid). When Subtotal and Payment agree on 102.00 but the keyword line reads 702.00, the outlier is still selected."},{"id":"R3","description":"The priority ordering between 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' and a final rounded 'TOTAL' line is ambiguous. Current skill text says 'take the last matching line' but the correct policy for this corpus appears to be: when both a GST-inclusive subtotal-style line AND a plain final rounded TOTAL exist, the GST-inclusive line is the gold answer unless the rounded line is explicitly labeled GRAND TOTAL."},{"id":"R4","description":"Date parser lacks a locale/order rule. For dd/mm/yyyy receipts (Malaysian GST receipts), the agent sometimes falls back to mm/dd/yyyy when the day digit <=12, producing swapped dates. Skill's DATE_PATTERNS list orders mm-dd before dd-mm or disambiguates incorrectly."},{"id":"R5","description":"Null handling is inconsistent: failures sometimes land in the Excel cell as '' (empty string) instead of actual None/empty cell, which the verifier treats as an incorrect value for the ground-truth null case."},{"id":"R6","description":"image-ocr SKILL.md does not codify these receipt-specific selection rules (anchor consensus, GST-inclusive preference, dd/mm default, strict None semantics), so the agent re-derived them ad hoc each iteration, overfitting to individual files and regressing on others."}],"skill_defects":[{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"Receipt total-selection policy is under-specified: no rule for picking among multiple keyword-matching lines in the same EXCLUDING/EXCL., SUBTOTAL, TAX/GST/SST, DISCOUNT, CHANGE, CASH TENDERED, ROUNDING ADJUSTMENT); (2) collect candidates per priority tier across 2-3 OCR variants; (3) within the top matched tier, prefer the value that is consistent with other anchor lines on the same receipt (Subtotal, Payment/Cash Received minus Change, Total Rounded) — if an anchor value appears ≥2 times among non-excluded lines, prefer the candidate equal to that anchor over any outlier even if the outlier is on a later keyword line; (4) when both a 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' line and a plain 'TOTAL' line exist and the plain Explicitly instruct: if two interpretations are both valid, choose the one where month<=12 under DD/MM. Reject dates with year outside 1990-2100 or impossible month>12 and return None."},{"target":"skills/image-ocr/SKILL.md","change":"Add explicit Null Contract: 'If a field cannot be extracted, store Python None, not empty string, not the literal string None, not NaN. Include a short example writing a 'results' sheet with ['filename','date','total_amount'] columns and None cells."},{"target":"skills/image-ocr/SKILL.md and skills/xlsx/SKILL.md","change":"Cross-reference each other: image-ocr should instruct that when producing tabular OCR output, delegate writing to xlsx skill guidance for null and string-format handling; xlsx should mention OCR tabular tasks as a canonical example of the string/null contract."}],"confidence":0.72}
